project_title: Temporal Legal Drift in the Indian Code
primary_research_question: Do LLM-based compliance systems correctly propagate legally applicable changes in Indian law over time?

research_questions.RQ1: Can Indian legislative history be reconstructed accurately enough to determine which provision version governs a scenario at a specified date?
research_questions.RQ2: Can legally material changes be distinguished from non-material textual changes using structured amendment representations?
research_questions.RQ3: Do LLM compliance assertions appropriately update when the legally applicable Indian provision changes?
research_questions.RQ4: Can evidence-grounded explanations identify the correct legal version, amendment, materiality, and compliance consequence?

core_novelty_position: A temporally versioned India Code benchmark and evaluation framework that tests whether LLM compliance reasoning correctly propagates legally material legislative changes, while distinguishing genuine legal drift from non-material textual change and grounding conclusions in authoritative evidence.

corpus.primary_source_family: India Code and other authoritative Indian legal sources

required_comparators: closest legal change and materiality benchmarks
recent temporal legal reasoning and changing-law benchmarks

blockers: minimum and desired benchmark targets not set
materiality dimension count not formally approved
